prompt:
Find real, peer-reviewed or preprint studies measuring how often large language models fabricate citations. Cite the papers and quote the fabrication rates they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
These are the studies I found, with the exact sentences from the relevant pages:

SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Of the 222 works cited in the GPT-3.5 papers, 55% are fabricated (Table 3)." | CLAIM: The study found that 55% of the GPT-3.5 citations were fabricated.
SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Within this set of documents, 55% of the GPT-3.5 citations but just 18% of the GPT-4 citations are fabricated." | CLAIM: The same study found that 18% of the GPT-4 citations were fabricated.
SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Across the 6 reviews, GPT-4o generated 176 citations; 35 (19.9%) were fabricated." | CLAIM: In this GPT-4o study, 19.9% of the generated citations were fabricated overall.
SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Fabrication rates differed significantly by disorder (χ22=13.7; P=.001), with higher rates for binge eating disorder (17/60, 28%) and body dysmorphic disorder (14/48, 29%) than for major depressive disorder (4/68, 6%)." | CLAIM: Fabrication rates varied by topic: 28% for binge eating disorder, 29% for body dysmorphic disorder, and 6% for major depressive disorder.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03299 | QUOTE: "Our results show that the observed hallucination rates span a fivefold range (between 11.4% and 56.8%) and are strongly shaped by model, domain, and prompt framing." | CLAIM: Across 10 commercially deployed LLMs, citation hallucination/fabrication rates ranged from 11.4% to 56.8%, depending on model, domain, and prompt framing.
SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/11/5/122 | QUOTE: "Our manual verification process identified eight instances of fabricated references." | CLAIM: In their examination of references in published papers, the authors found eight instances of fabricated references.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: A direct percentage fabrication rate from the MDPI paper based on those eight instances (the provided page text did not state the percentage).

I’m relying on the page text you provided rather than independently re-verifying the underlying papers.
